expects.rule: Plan your visit information (opening hours, prices, accessibility, current programme) is easy to find. A 2026 benchmark of 50 cultural institution sites found Plan Your Visit pages scored lowest of all page types, 67.8 on average.
Design for the phone first: the same benchmark measured mobile performance at 40.6 against 57.8 on desktop, a gap of 17.2 points. The source is a hosting vendor, so treat the figures as indicative.
Ticketing and event discovery have as few steps as possible. The benchmark says leading museums remove friction there.
Audio that starts on its own for more than 3 seconds comes with a control to pause or stop it, or to set its volume separately from the system volume (WCAG 2.2 criterion 1.4.2).
Each exhibition, concert or show page states its dates and times as text, with the venue and a booking link.
Artists and labels put the latest release or next date in the first screen, with the streaming or ticket link one click away.
Collections and archives are searchable text with image descriptions, not only large images.

traits: 5 of 8 first screens are led by a photograph or artwork of people (Van Morrison, Rude Ingénierie, NY Phil, Die Antwoord, Lady Gaga); Kalkbrenner uses a small portrait inside the name.
The name or title is the largest element on 5 of 8, between 133 and 201 px or spanning the width (Kalkbrenner, Van Morrison, NY Phil, Die Antwoord, Lady Gaga).
Text on the first screen stays under 40 words on 6 of 8; Kalkbrenner, Die Antwoord, OSI and Sleutelaar carry one line or none.
5 of 8 use black or near-black as the page colour (Van Morrison, Rude Ingénierie, Die Antwoord, Lady Gaga, NY Phil header); the rest are white, pale grey or a single flat colour.
3 of 8 open with a loader or an intro that must finish before content shows (OSI, Sleutelaar, and Rude Ingénierie's moving grid).
4 of 8 put practical or commercial links in the first screen: Get Tickets and Donate (NY Phil), Subscribe and Order vinyl (Van Morrison), Shop and Cart (Lady Gaga), Store (Kalkbrenner).
Audio is integrated but controlled: Kalkbrenner shows 'Sound OFF', OSI asks the visitor to turn audio on, as WCAG 1.4.2 expects.

sites.name: Paul Kalkbrenner
sites.why: White page with the name 'Paul Kalkbrenner' at 133 px in bold ABC Diatype, a small black-and-white portrait inserted between the two words; menu of eight items across the top, a 'Now playing' track control and 'Sound OFF' at the bottom, one sentence of text. One typeface, no colour.

sites.name: Van Morrison
sites.why: Full-bleed photograph of the singer at a keyboard on a pink curtain, 'VAN MORRISON' at 201 px in white Oswald, a three-link menu with streaming icons and a Subscribe button, an orange card for a vinyl and CD release (Order vinyl and CD). Cookie box at left. Inria Serif for text.

sites.name: Théâtre Rude Ingénierie
sites.why: Near-black (#0a0600) field of square photographs of stage shows, drifting and mixed with red squares; company name at top, Menu and Liste links, filters (Tout, Immersifs, Installations) at the bottom. Titles such as Libre // Dire oui show over images. One typeface (Host Grotesk).

sites.name: New York Philharmonic, Welcome Gustavo
sites.why: Black header with the orchestra's logo, Donate, account and search, 'Get Tickets' and 'Full Calendar' links; below, a yellow panel with 'NEW YORK'S NEW MAESTRO' in a black condensed face around a cut-out conductor in a black box. Cookie bar at the bottom.

sites.name: OSI 90th Anniversary
sites.why: Pale grey (#e4e6e7) screen with soft pink and orange gradients and faint vertical lines; only the small 90 OSI logo and the line 'Celebriamo 89 anni, per un'esperienza ottimale attiva l'audio'. Almarena Display type. No menu on the loading screen.

sites.name: Archive for Hans Sleutelaar
sites.why: On capture only a near-black (#0d0d0d) screen with a thin progress line, the word SLEUTELAAR and a counter (71); the loaded page is white with a menu (Biografie, Index, Gedichten, Archief) and a short Dutch biography in ABC Monument Grotesk (not seen beyond the loader).

sites.name: DIE ANTWOORD
sites.why: Black bars above and below a split screen: a grey painted portrait of the two members on the left with the band name in a ragged white face, a flat orange painted panel on the right with 'ZAMA ZAMA' and 'World tour 2027, watch this space'. No menu, no text beyond those lines.

sites.name: Lady Gaga, A Digital Home for a Global Pop Icon
sites.why: Full-bleed red-tinted video of a face with glitch lines; 'A YEAR OF' in a serif and 'MAYHEM' in a distressed white display face, menu (Latest, Music, Shop, Projects, Live), Account, Cart, a strip of about 20 release thumbnails at the bottom, cookie box at left.
sites.recognition: Webby Award 2025, Entertainment, General Desktop & Mobile Sites

avoid: Opening hours, prices or the programme only inside an image or a PDF.
Music that starts on arrival with no visible pause control.
A full-screen intro animation the visitor must wait for before reaching dates or tickets.
Embedding a third-party streaming widget as the only content of the home page.
Large uncaptioned images with no text alternative, so the collection cannot be read by a screen reader.
A Plan your visit page buried in the footer on a museum site.

sources.name: Pantheon and Urban Insight, State of Museum Digital 2026 benchmark
Awwwards, Culture & Education and Music & Sound
